title: Softr Pricing 2026: Plans, Limits, and Features
summary: Softr pricing plans vary by workflow actions, the limit most teams hit first. Review each tier to pick the plan your team won't outgrow.
body_markdown:
## How all Softr plans compare


Softr sells four plans: Free, Basic, Pro and Business. Each is defined by the same nine measures: monthly price, annual price, users, apps, records, workflow runs, custom domain, SSO and support. **Whichever measure runs out first decides your plan** .


### The plan table, checked against Softr's pricing page


Softr's pricing page was checked on 2 November 2026, and it's the only place to read the live figures for those nine measures.


This section doesn't copy the numbers across.


### Softr plan quantity limits and feature gates


Read the nine measures in two groups. Users, apps, records and workflow runs are quantities, so they run out gradually as you grow. **Custom domain, SSO and support are gates** : your plan either includes them or it doesn't.


You can plan around a quantity. A gate stops you cold, usually on the day a client asks for single sign-on or wants the portal on their own web address. Mark which gates you need before you compare any prices.


### Softr monthly versus annual billing prices


Each paid plan shows two prices, one for paying month to month and one for paying a year at a time.


The headline figure on the page may be the annual one, so check which of the two you're looking at before you compare Softr with anything else.


Annual billing usually lowers the monthly cost, but it commits you for the year. If you're still testing whether Softr suits the job, month to month costs more per month and lets you leave.


### What the free plan really allows


Build and test on the Free plan; don't try to run a business on it. Treat it as a trial with no deadline: build your app, load a realistic sample of your data, and see which limit you hit first.


Pay attention to what is missing as much as to what is included. If you need a custom domain, SSO or workflow runs at volume, check whether Free has them at all. If it doesn't, you've found your upgrade trigger before spending anything.


If the trigger you find is the 500-action ceiling, the real cost is that pricing by headcount and volume decides who gets to automate at all: the tool goes to a chosen few, and everyone else waits in a queue that never clears.


Activepieces charges for use rather than seats, so a new person costs nothing until they run something, and a run is 1 credit however many steps it has.


Unlimited flows come on every plan, the free one included with its 1,000 credits a month, and Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.
